outcomes: A workload declares a configuration block once and reads it as a validated, typed value
The same declaration behaves identically in every environment because precedence between sources is fixed
A secret is declared beside the value it protects and never appears in a log, an error, a description, or a committed manifest
A browser build reads the same declaration without pretending it has server configuration sources
nonGoals: Reloading configuration in a running process when a file or environment variable changes
Storing, distributing, or rotating secret values
Promising that a pre-1.0 minor release keeps the previous precedence order

requirements.text: Configuration sources merge from lowest to highest as base file, environment file, build-merged file, local secrets file, registered extension sources, then CONFIG_DATA.
A field-level Env() descriptor supplies a value only when no merged source provided that key, so any file or CONFIG_DATA value overrides the environment variable.
A missing required field or a value that does not match its declared type fails the read instead of yielding a partially valid configuration object.
A field declared Sensitive() is redacted in validation errors and in the config description, including when it is nested inside another block.
Emitted infrastructure requirements carry the canonicalized names of sensitive fields and never their values, and the sidecar is removed when no sensitive field remains.
Parsed configuration cannot pollute Object.prototype: __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys are stripped from every source before merging.
A dependency-contributed config block registers under its own path; re-registering the identical definition is a no-op and a different definition claiming the same path fails.

The browser entry point applies declared defaults and call-site overrides, reports the browser environment, and never reads files, CONFIG_DATA, or environment variables nor throws on a missing required field.
